newsitem.title: UK: Direct response insurers to expand in US -report.
newsitem.headline: Direct response insurers to expand in US -report.

text.p: Direct response insurers, or tele-underwriters, are set to increase their share of the personal automotive market in the U.S. to 10.5 percent by 2000 from 8.5 percent in 1995, management consultant Datamonitor said on Monday.

"Datamonitor's forecasts have predicted that tele-underwriters will see the strongest growth in market share over the next few years," the London-based consultancy said in its report 'The Future of US Telefinancial Services'.
In the U.S., direct writers are insurers which distribute exclusively or predominantly through a captive sales force. They controlled 59.3 percent of the personal auto market in 1995.
A direct response operator is an insurer which sells insurance predominantly over the telephone, and is able to quote and provide cover over the telephone.
Direct response insurers have expanded rapidly in the last two years in personal auto and had net premiums written last year of $9.5 billion, compared with $8.7 billion in 1995.

The largest direct response insurer, United Services Automobile Association, had 3.3 percent of the total market. Direct response insurers achieved an 8.9 percent growth rate last year, against 5.4 percent for the market as a whole.
Direct response insurers have an average price advantage of 27.2 percent over agency insurers, and are making gains largely at the expense of insurance agents, Datamonitor said.
It expects agents' market share to fall to 26.7 percent in 2000 from 29.3 percent in 1995.
